newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - SFE wheat turns active in distant spreads.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - SFE wheat turns active in distant spreads.

text.p: Wheat futures trading turned active on the Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) on Wednesday as spread trading dominated in distant contracts.
A total of 48 futures trades took place, well up on the low-volumes of recent weeks.
January 1997 fell by A$1.50 on the trade to A$168.00, November fell 50 cents to A$167.00, January 1998 rose A$2.00 to A$165.00 and the new March 1998 contract was steady on A$163.00.
"There's a fair bit of spreading about the place," Brendon Hillary of ANZ McCaughan Futures Ltd said. This brought the market in back month contracts into line," he said.
After some two-way business between A$168.00 and A$170.00, January 1997 closed down A$2.00 to A$167.50 on settlement.
This was likely to anticipate Chicago tonight, Hillary said.
Stories of "a heap of wheat around the world" should not come as a surprise because they only echoed what was already known, he said. "It's just coming to fruition now."
But importing countries were still on the sidelines waiting to see how cheap wheat could get, he said.
China's purchase of about 700,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat and Egypt's purchase of 450,000 tonnes of French wheat were bearish because they were traditionally U.S. customers, he said.
